newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 20.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Government officials and New Korea Party members hinted on Sunday they will adopt concilatory measures to solve the present strike crisis in the nation as soon as possible.
- The government has decided to excercise maximum flexibility if North Korea decides to enter four-way talks between the two Koreas, China and the United States.
- President Kim Young-sam met with leaders of the nation's Protestant churches at Chong Wa Dae Saturday to hear their opinion on ways to defuse the current labour crisis.

- After Taiwan's rejection of South Korea's demands to call off planned shipments of nuclear waste to North Korea, Seoul is planning a diplomatic front composed of China, Japan and the United States to pressure Taiwan, a government official said.
- The United States has requested South Korea adopt calming measures to solve the present industrial crisis, including ammending the controversial new labour law, a high-level government source said.
- Employment in the manufacturing sector is falling drastically. The number of employees in the sector now accounts for 21 percent of the total workforce against 26 percent in 1991.
